title: What If Earth Were Twice as Wide? You'd Weigh Double

scenes.text: What if Earth were twice as wide? You would weigh double, and that is only the start.
Double the diameter means about eight times the mass, if it is made of the same rock.
Surface gravity is mass divided by radius squared. Eight divided by four is two.
So a 150-pound person would weigh 300 pounds on the same ground.
Scientists who imagined this world say tall trees like redwoods could not stand, and animals would need thicker legs.
Planets that heavy do exist elsewhere. On one candidate with eight Earth masses, you would weigh about 1.4 times more.
